description: Our team is addressing the NASA Space Apps Challenge: Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions. Deep-space exploration, prolonged microgravity, and communication delays to ground medical control demand autonomous, reliable on-station health telemetry.
summary: VITALITY is an advanced, offline-first deep-space health monitoring and autonomous medical triage web application engineered for long-duration missions. Developed to combat multi-minute communication delays with Earth, VITALITY features secure mission authentication across 5 distinct flights, a real-time interactive 3D lung respiratory simulation with microgravity stress modes, and a dynamic telemetry dashboard tracking vital physiological metrics. By enabling autonomous anomaly detection and crew health oversight, VITALITY ensures astronaut safety and mission success far beyond Earth’s orbit.
details:
What Does It Do or How Does It Work?

VITALITY is an advanced, offline-first deep-space health monitoring and autonomous medical triage web application designed for long-duration space missions.

  • How it works: It features secure mission authentication configured across 5 distinct space missions (supporting 3 crew members per flight, such as Commander, Mission Specialist/Medical Officer, and Pilot), a real-time interactive 3D lung respiratory simulation with normal and microgravity stress modes, and a dynamic telemetry dashboard tracking vital physiological metrics (heart rate, blood pressure, core body temperature, and blood oxygen levels). It operates entirely offline to provide autonomous triage and anomaly detection without relying on ground control.

What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Autonomous Reliability: Functions independently during multi-minute communication delays between deep-space vessels and Earth.
  • Early Hazard Detection: Continuously tracks physiological signs to identify early indicators of spaceflight hazards like cardiovascular deconditioning and microgravity stress.
  • Multi-Mission Scalability: Easily switches between crew profiles and flight identifiers to manage multiple astronauts simultaneously.

What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

The primary impact of VITALITY is safeguarding astronaut well-being and enhancing crew autonomy during deep-space exploration far beyond Earth’s orbit. By bridging the gap between raw biometric telemetry and actionable medical decision support, the system ensures that crew members can swiftly triage health emergencies and maintain peak operational readiness.

What Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, or Software Did You Use?

  • Languages & Frameworks: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Three.js for 3D graphics rendering.
  • Development Tools & Environment: Visual Studio Code on Windows, GitHub, and GitHub Pages for live web hosting.
  • Data & Clinical Frameworks: Grounded in NASA Open Science data frameworks, leveraging parameters and risk mitigation protocols inspired by the Life Sciences Data Archive (LSDA), Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), and Human Research Roadmap (HRR).

How Is Your Project Creative?

VITALITY stands out by blending a fully immersive, interactive 3D space-themed UI and respiratory simulation with rigorous, data-driven medical monitoring. Instead of a static dashboard, it features real-time microgravity stress toggles, custom multi-mission authentication gates, and dynamic telemetry visualizers tailored specifically for the extreme conditions of spaceflight.

What Factors Did Your Team Consider?

  • Communication Latency: Designed entirely offline-first to combat deep-space signal delays where real-time Earth support is impossible.
  • Spaceflight Hazards: Evaluated physiological risks specific to long-duration missions—such as respiratory shifts in microgravity—and mapped them directly to interactive UI states.
  • Crew Usability: Prioritized high-contrast, easily scannable data panels and quick-switching crew profiles (CDR, MS, PLT) to ensure clarity during high-stress operational scenarios.
